en: judge; rule on a case; give a verdict

examples.en: The court ruled on the case today.
The judge rules based on the evidence.

examples.ko: 판결할 때는 모든 사실을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to check all the facts when you pass judgment.

examples.ko: 재판부가 무죄로 판결하면 피고는 바로 풀려나요.
examples.en: If the court rules not guilty, the defendant is released right away.
This issue is hard to settle in court.

examples.ko: 법원이 어떻게 판결할지 모두 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is waiting to see how the court will rule.

explain: 판결하다는 재판에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 일상에서 무언가를 정할 때는 '결정하다'나 '정하다'를 써요. 보통 '판결을 내리다'처럼 명사와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: This is a courtroom word and rarely appears in everyday talk. For ordinary decisions Koreans say '결정하다' or '정하다'. It is usually paired with the noun, as in '판결을 내리다'.

en: be closed (when a deadline passes or spots fill up)

examples.en: Applications closed yesterday.
Registration closes this evening.
Hand in the documents before it closes.
Recruitment had closed, so I couldn't apply.
I didn't know the event had closed.
Once registration closes, they don't accept anyone more.

explain: 마감하다는 사람이 끝내는 것이고, 마감되다는 시간이나 인원이 다 차서 저절로 끝나는 거예요. 명사 '마감'으로 '마감일', '마감 시간'처럼 더 많이 써요. 자리가 다 찼을 때도 '선착순 마감'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '마감하다' is something a person does to wrap things up, while '마감되다' happens by itself when time runs out or spots fill up. The noun '마감' is more common, as in '마감일' or '마감 시간'. Full spots are also called '선착순 마감'.

examples.en: I'm so ashamed that my lie was found out.

examples.ko: 그는 수치스러운 기억을 잊고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: He wants to forget his humiliating memory.
It was humiliating to get it wrong in front of people.
I was so ashamed that my face turned red.
I think that kind of behavior is shameful.

examples.ko: 저는 수치스럽지 않은 삶을 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to live a life I'm not ashamed of.

explain: 일상에서는 '창피하다'를 훨씬 자주 쓰고, 수치스럽다는 더 무겁고 글에 가까워요. 가벼운 실수에는 '창피해요'가 자연스러워요. '부끄럽다'는 마음속에서 느끼는 감정이고, 수치스럽다는 남 앞에서 체면이 크게 상한 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: In daily speech '창피하다' is far more common; '수치스럽다' is heavier and more bookish. For small slips, '창피해요' sounds natural. '부끄럽다' is an inner feeling, while '수치스럽다' stresses a serious loss of face in front of others.

examples.en: I'm truly honored to receive the award.

examples.ko: 오늘 이 자리에 서게 되어 영광스러웠어요.
examples.en: It was an honor to stand here today.
I captured the glorious moment in a photo.

examples.ko: 선생님과 함께 일하는 것은 영광스러운 일이에요.
examples.en: Working with you is an honor.
I was so honored that I cried.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 대표하게 되면 영광스러울 거예요.
examples.en: It will be an honor if I get to represent our team.

explain: 인사말에서는 '영광이에요', '영광입니다'를 더 자주 써요. 영광스럽다는 형용사라서 '영광스러운 일'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요. 높은 사람이나 큰 행사에서 감사를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: In greetings Koreans more often say '영광이에요' or '영광입니다'. '영광스럽다' is an adjective, so it can modify a noun, as in '영광스러운 일'. It fits when thanking someone senior or speaking at a big event.

examples.en: The notice was handed out to all students.
The new version will be released tomorrow.
Masks are being handed out for free.
I'll tell you by email once the materials are out.
A wrong file got released, and now we're in trouble.
Please update the released app now.

explain: 배포하다의 피동이에요. 누가 나눠 줬는지보다 나눠졌다는 사실이 중요할 때 써요. 공지, 뉴스, 앱 업데이트 소식에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '배포하다'. Use it when the fact that something went out matters more than who sent it. It shows up often in notices, news, and app update announcements.

examples.en: The school handed out notices to the students.
The company releases the new app for free.

examples.ko: 파일을 배포하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check once more before you release the file.
City Hall will hand out maps to citizens.
You must not distribute these materials.

examples.ko: 우리가 만든 프로그램을 인터넷에 배포하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are releasing the program we made on the internet.

explain: '나눠 주다'보다 딱딱한 말이에요. 종이를 손으로 줄 때는 '나눠 주다'가 일상적이고, 자료나 프로그램을 많은 사람에게 내놓을 때는 배포하다를 써요. IT 쪽에서는 소프트웨어를 내놓는 일도 배포라고 해요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '나눠 주다'. For paper handed out by hand, '나눠 주다' is the everyday choice, while 배포하다 fits materials or programs offered to many people. In IT, releasing software is also called 배포.

examples.en: Today's game is broadcast live on TV.
The final was broadcast around the world.
The concert is being broadcast live.
The live screen keeps cutting out.
This event is not broadcast live.
Shall we watch the game together when it's broadcast?

explain: 스포츠나 행사를 현장에서 바로 보여 줄 때 써요. 일상에서는 명사 '중계'나 '생중계'를 더 자주 들어요. 방송하는 쪽은 '중계하다', 방송되는 경기나 행사 쪽은 중계되다예요.
explain_en: It is used when a sport or event is shown live from the scene. In daily life you more often hear the nouns '중계' and '생중계'. The broadcasting side uses '중계하다', while the game or event being shown is '중계되다'.

examples.en: Experts estimate that the damage is large.
It's hard to estimate the exact age.

examples.ko: 경찰은 사고 시간을 밤 열 시쯤으로 추정했어요.
examples.en: The police estimated the accident happened around ten at night.

examples.ko: 값을 추정할 때는 비슷한 물건과 비교해요.
examples.en: When I estimate a price, I compare it with similar items.

examples.ko: 자료를 보면 손님이 늘 것으로 추정돼요.
examples.en: The data suggests that customers will increase.
What's your reason for presuming that?

explain: '짐작하다'는 가볍게 생각해 보는 거고, 추정하다는 자료나 근거로 계산하거나 판단한다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스에서 숫자와 함께 '~로 추정돼요'를 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아마 ~일 것 같아요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '짐작하다' is a casual guess, while 추정하다 suggests judging from data or evidence. News often says '~로 추정돼요' next to numbers. In daily talk, '아마 ~일 것 같아요' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 두 장을 합성한 거예요.
examples.en: This photo is a composite of two pictures.
I tried combining face photos with an app.

examples.ko: 두 물질을 합성하면 새로운 재료가 돼요.
examples.en: If you synthesize two substances, you get a new material.
I'm learning how to composite videos.
They synthesized a voice to make the announcement.
I can't tell if it's a composite picture or a real one.

explain: 여러 개를 합쳐 하나로 만든다는 말인데, 사진·영상·소리·화학 물질에 쓰여요. 일상에서는 사진 합성이 가장 흔해요. 그냥 '합치다'와 달리 새로운 결과물이 나온다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means combining several things into one, used for photos, video, sound, and chemical substances. In daily life, photo compositing is the most common use. Unlike plain '합치다', it implies a new product comes out.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 상대 공격을 잘 방어했어요.
examples.en: Our team defended well against the other side's attack.
The goalkeeper stops the last shot.
I covered my face with my arms to protect myself.
I work on defending systems from hackers.
The lawyer will defend the client to the end.
You can't win just by defending.

explain: 일상에서 '막다'를 많이 쓰고, 방어하다는 스포츠·군사·보안에서 주로 써요. 반대말은 '공격하다'예요. 팀 경기에서 자리를 지키는 일은 '수비하다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: In daily life '막다' is common; 방어하다 is mostly for sports, military, and security. The opposite is '공격하다'. For holding a position in team games, '수비하다' is used even more.

examples.en: The police are tracking the suspect's location.
I'll trace where the package is now.
This app tracks your step count.
The reporter followed the case for a long time.

examples.ko: 발자국을 추적하면 길을 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you follow the footprints, you can find the way.
It's hard to track once the phone is off.

explain: '쫓다'는 눈앞의 사람이나 동물을 따라가는 느낌이고, 추적하다는 흔적이나 기록을 따라가며 찾는 거예요. 택배 조회를 '배송 추적'이라고 해요. 목적어로 사람, 위치, 기록이 모두 올 수 있어요.
explain_en: '쫓다' means chasing someone in front of you, while 추적하다 means following traces or records to find something. Checking a parcel is called '배송 추적'. The object can be a person, a location, or a record.

examples.en: A referee has to be fair to all players.
The result was fair, so no one complained.
The teacher treats students fairly.
I felt the test wasn't fair.
We decided to split the cost fairly.
If the competition is fair, I'll accept the result.

explain: '공평하다'는 똑같이 나눈다는 느낌이고, 공정하다는 규칙과 기준이 올바르다는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '불공정하다'예요. 사람, 심판, 시험, 경쟁에 자주 써요.
explain_en: '공평하다' feels like dividing things equally, while 공정하다 feels like the rules and standards are right. The opposite is '불공정하다'. It is often used for people, referees, tests, and competition.

examples.en: People resisted the unfair order.
The child resists because they don't want to go to the hospital.
If you resist change, things get harder.
He didn't resist to the end.
I walked, pushing against the strong wind.
Germs that resist medicine are increasing.

explain: '버티다'는 참고 견디는 느낌이고, 저항하다는 상대의 힘이나 명령에 맞선다는 느낌이에요. 조사는 '~에 저항하다'를 써요. 명사 '저항'은 '저항이 크다', '저항을 받다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '버티다' is about enduring, while 저항하다 is about standing against someone's force or order. The particle is '에', as in '~에 저항하다'. The noun '저항' appears in '저항이 크다' and '저항을 받다'.

en: be killed in action; die in battle

examples.en: My grandfather's older brother was killed in the war.

examples.ko: 그 군인은 용감히 싸우다 전사했다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that soldier fell fighting bravely.
There is a day to remember the fallen soldiers.
Many soldiers died in battle, and people grieved.
He wrote a letter to his family before dying in battle.
The hero in the movie dies in battle at the end.

explain: 전쟁에서 싸우다 죽는 것에만 써요. 사고나 병으로 죽을 때는 '죽다'나 높임말 '돌아가시다'를 써요. 역사 이야기와 뉴스에서 나와요.
explain_en: It is only for dying while fighting in a war. For death by accident or illness, use '죽다' or the honorific '돌아가시다'. You meet it in history stories and the news.

en: be put in; be thrown in; be deployed

examples.en: The rescue team was sent to the scene right away.
A new player comes on in the second half.
A lot of money was put into this project.

examples.ko: 신입 직원이 팀에 투입되면 먼저 교육을 받아요.
examples.en: When a new employee joins a team, they get training first.

examples.ko: 투입된 인원이 너무 적어서 일이 느려요.
examples.en: The work is slow because too few people were assigned.
The order in which materials are put in matters.

explain: 투입하다의 피동이에요. 사람이 어떤 자리에 보내질 때는 '현장에 투입되다'라고 해요. 스포츠에서 교체 선수가 경기에 나가는 것도 투입이에요. '돈이 투입되다'처럼 물건과 돈도 주어가 돼요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '투입하다'. When a person is sent to a post, we say '현장에 투입되다'. A substitute going onto the field in sports is also 투입. Money and materials can be the subject too, as in '돈이 투입되다'.

en: put in; throw in; deploy; invest

examples.en: The company put a lot of money into the new business.
The coach sends in a new player in the second half.

examples.ko: 사람을 더 투입하면 일이 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If we put in more people, the work finishes faster.

examples.ko: 소방대가 불을 끄려고 헬기를 투입할 거래요.
examples.en: I hear the fire department will send in a helicopter to put out the fire.
Check before you put the materials into the machine.

examples.ko: 시간을 많이 투입한 만큼 결과가 좋아요.
examples.en: The result is good in proportion to the time put in.

explain: 돈, 사람, 시간, 장비처럼 일에 필요한 것을 넣을 때 써요. '넣다'보다 딱딱하고 계획적인 느낌이에요. '인력을 투입하다', '예산을 투입하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: Use it for putting in what a job needs: money, people, time, equipment. It is stiffer and more planned than '넣다'. Common pairs are '인력을 투입하다' and '예산을 투입하다'.

examples.en: Our team won the gold medal.
In the game, your score goes up when you obtain an item.
It takes time to earn people's trust.
The goal is to gain a lot of support.
There's no way to obtain that information.

examples.ko: 점수를 획득한 사람만 다음 단계로 가요.
examples.en: Only those who earned points go to the next stage.

explain: '얻다'와 같은 뜻이지만, 노력해서 손에 넣은 결과에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 게임의 '아이템 획득', 경기의 '메달 획득'이 자주 보여요. 자격증이나 면허는 보통 '취득하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means about the same as '얻다', but it is a stiffer word for something gained through effort. You often see '아이템 획득' in games and '메달 획득' in sports. For certificates or licenses, '취득하다' is the usual verb.

examples.en: I applied to have a dashcam installed on my new car.
Fitting the tires takes about thirty minutes.
Be sure to check whether the helmet is on.
The parts have been fitted onto the machine.
The installation method is in the manual.
Installing the safety device has become mandatory.

explain: 보통 '장착하다', '장착되다'로 더 자주 써요. 명사 장착은 '타이어 장착', '장착 완료'처럼 다른 말 앞뒤에 붙여 말해요. 일상에서는 '달다', '끼우다'가 더 쉬운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is more often used as the verbs '장착하다' and '장착되다'. As a noun it attaches to other words, as in '타이어 장착' or '장착 완료'. In everyday speech '달다' and '끼우다' are the easier words.

examples.en: This building is rented out as offices.
The empty shop was rented out last month.

examples.ko: 임대된 집은 마음대로 고치면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not alter a rented house as you like.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 오 년 동안 임대될 예정이에요.
examples.en: This land is scheduled to be leased for five years.

examples.ko: 임대되기 전에 집을 한번 보러 갈까요?
examples.en: Shall we go see the house before it's rented out?
The car is already rented out, so it's not here now.

explain: 임대는 집주인이 빌려주는 쪽의 말이고, 빌리는 쪽은 '임차'라고 해요. 그래서 집이 임대되었다는 말은 누군가 빌려 쓰고 있다는 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '세를 놓다', '월세로 나오다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '임대' is the lender's side, and the borrower's side is '임차'. So a house described as 임대되다 is now being rented by someone. In everyday speech '세를 놓다' and '월세로 나오다' are also common.

en: be maintained; be overhauled; be put in order

examples.en: The park paths have been newly redone.

examples.ko: 차가 잘 정비돼 있어서 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: The car is well maintained, so I feel safe.
Once the rules are put in order, confusion will decrease.
Many people exercise along the redeveloped riverside.
All planes are inspected before departure.
It took several years for the system to be put in order.

explain: 정비하다의 피동이에요. 길, 시설, 제도가 정리되고 새로워졌다는 말로 뉴스에 많이 나와요. '정비된 도로'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '정비하다'. It appears a lot in the news for roads, facilities, or systems that have been tidied up and renewed. It also works as a modifier, as in '정비된 도로'.

examples.en: The mechanic is servicing the plane.
I went to the garage to get my car serviced.
The city redid the old road.
We need to put the rules in order again.
I'll use the equipment again after servicing it.
We service the machines every month.

explain: '고치다'는 고장 난 것을 수리하는 거고, 정비하다는 문제가 생기기 전에 점검하고 손봐서 잘 쓸 수 있게 만드는 거예요. 차, 비행기뿐 아니라 길, 규칙, 제도에도 써요. 자동차 가게 이름에 '정비'가 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '고치다' is fixing something broken, while 정비하다 is checking and adjusting things before problems arise so they work well. It applies to cars and planes but also to roads, rules, and systems. You often see '정비' in auto shop names.

en: be shut down; be closed off

examples.en: The road was closed because of an accident.
That factory was shut down last year.
The gate is closed off, so we can't get in.
If the park is closed, where will we exercise?
I don't know why my account was closed.
There is a school that will be closed down next month.

explain: '닫히다'는 문이 닫히는 가벼운 말이고, 폐쇄되다는 공식적으로 또는 오랫동안 막힌다는 뜻이에요. 도로, 공장, 학교, 계정처럼 큰 대상에 써요. 가게가 문을 닫는 것은 '폐업하다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '닫히다' is the light word for a door closing, while 폐쇄되다 means being shut officially or for a long time. It suits big things like roads, factories, schools, and accounts. A shop going out of business is more often '폐업하다'.

examples.en: The city closed the dangerous bridge.
I hear the company is shutting down the regional factory.
They decided to close the school down.
The police are sealing off the accident site.
If you close the account, all the data disappears.
They sealed the entrance, so no one can leave.

explain: '닫다'보다 공식적이고 크게 막는다는 느낌이에요. 가게는 '폐업하다', 학교는 '폐교하다'처럼 대상마다 따로 쓰는 말도 있어요. 반대말은 '개방하다'예요.
explain_en: It feels more official and larger in scale than '닫다'. Some targets have their own words, like '폐업하다' for a shop and '폐교하다' for a school. The opposite is '개방하다'.

examples.en: The hero saved the villagers.

examples.ko: 위험에 빠진 아이들을 구원한 소방관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a firefighter who rescued children in danger.
I felt that music saved me.
Who will save this country?

examples.ko: 위기에 빠진 회사를 구원하고 싶어서 직접 나섰어요.
examples.en: I stepped in myself because I wanted to save the company from the crisis.

examples.ko: 종교가 사람을 구원한다고 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe religion saves people.

explain: 일상에서는 '구하다', '도와주다'를 쓰고, 구원하다는 큰 위기나 종교에서 사람을 건진다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 영화나 소설에서 '세상을 구원하다'처럼 나와요. 작은 도움에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: In daily life Koreans say '구하다' or '도와주다'; 구원하다 carries a heavy sense of rescuing someone from a great crisis or in a religious sense. It appears in films and novels, as in '세상을 구원하다'. It does not suit small favors.
